title: Property guidance for protein sequence generative models with ProteinGuide - Nature Biotechnology
gist: ProteinGuide is a UC Berkeley method for steering pretrained protein generative models (ESM3, ProteinMPNN, MultiFlow) toward user-specified properties at inference time, with no fine-tuning of the generative model. Its headline wet-lab result is an adenine base editor with higher in vivo editing efficiency than a variant produced by seven rounds of directed evolution, achieved in two rounds of library design; it also handles two properties in direct tension (higher Pb binding, lower off-target Zn binding). The code, package and a practical usage guide are open, and the authors sit at Scribe Therapeutics, Generate:Biomedicines and Fable Therapeutics.

insights.claim: Before ProteinGuide there was no principled framework for conditioning protein sequence generative models on auxiliary information such as experimental assay data without additionally training the generative model itself.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Protein-design platforms whose differentiation is 'we fine-tune the foundation model on our data' lose that moat if inference-time guidance matches it at a fraction of the compute.
insights.quote: No principled framework exists for conditioning sequence generative models for protein engineering on auxiliary information, such as experimental data, without additional training of a generative model.

insights.claim: ProteinGuide derives from a unifying statistical framework that covers masked language models, any-order autoregressive models, and discrete-state diffusion and flow-matching models as a single class, so one guidance method spans architectures that are usually treated as separate research lines.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Architecture bets in protein AI matter less than assumed; the guidance layer is portable, which favors companies owning data and assays over those owning a specific backbone model.
insights.quote: ProteinGuide is amenable to a broad class of protein generative models including masked language models such as ESM3, any-order autoregressive models such as ProteinMPNN and diffusion and flow-matching models on discrete state-spaces

insights.claim: The method is positioned explicitly against RL, DPO and reward fine-tuning approaches to steering protein models, all of which require touching the generative model's weights and risk catastrophic forgetting and fine-tuning instability.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Signals that the protein-design field is converging on the same conclusion as text LLMs — steer at sampling time, keep the base model frozen — which compresses the compute cost of iterating design campaigns.
insights.locator: References, Aligning protein generative models with experimental fitness

insights.claim: ProteinGuide combined with in-house wet-lab data produced an adenine base editor with higher in vivo editing efficiency than the best variant previously obtained through seven rounds of directed evolution.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete head-to-head where ML design beats the incumbent protein-engineering workflow on a commercially central asset class — base editors sit inside Beam-, Prime- and Scribe-style gene-editing pipelines.
insights.quote: resulting in a base editor with higher editing efficiency than was previously achieved using seven rounds of directed evolution

insights.claim: The base-editor campaign converged in only two rounds of library generation, with round-one enrichment data used to train a classifier at a log-enrichment class boundary that then guided round-two designs.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Two rounds versus seven collapses the timeline and burn of an enzyme-optimization program; the economic argument for ML-guided engineering is cycle count, not just hit quality.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 7, Experimental log enrichments of the sequences in the first round libraries

insights.claim: Enrichment was measured across n = 2 biological replicates in round one and n = 3 in round two, with designs tracked by both mutational distance from wild-type TadA and by which generative model produced them.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Replicate counts are low, so the efficiency claim rests on a modest experimental base — worth checking before extrapolating to therapeutic editors.

insights.claim: Plasmids for the engineered base editors are being deposited through Addgene under the Savage lab and raw sequencing data released via BioProject PRJNA1467757, making the improved editor immediately available to academic and commercial groups.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open deposition means the editing-efficiency gain diffuses fast; competitive advantage in gene editing shifts to delivery and clinical execution rather than editor potency.

insights.claim: ProteinGuide was used to optimize two properties in direct tension simultaneously — increasing lead binding while reducing off-target zinc binding in the PbrR sensor protein — rather than optimizing a single fitness scalar.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Selectivity, not raw potency, is the binding problem in most therapeutic and sensor programs; a method that handles Pareto trade-offs natively is more useful than one that maximizes affinity.
insights.quote: Proteins are additionally designed to optimize for two desired properties that are in tension with each other.

insights.claim: The PbrR task was set up as Pareto-extrapolative: the guidance model was pushed into a target region of property space beyond the training data, and benchmarked against a fine-tuned model and a prior multi-objective method rather than against random sampling.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Extrapolation beyond the assay envelope is where design methods usually fail; benchmarking there is the honest test and the one to demand from vendors.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 6, Multi-property, Pareto-extrapolative experiment

insights.claim: ProteinMPNN guided by experimental stability data generated sequences that were still diverse and novel relative to the labeled dataset, measured by pairwise Hamming distance and minimum distance to known sequences.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Guidance that collapses library diversity is worthless for downstream screening; explicit diversity/novelty reporting is the metric to demand in design-platform diligence.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 3, Diversity and novelty of generated sequences

insights.claim: ESM3 was guided by assay-informed predictive models to perform extrapolative design, showing the method works when the conditioning signal is a learned oracle rather than direct measurements.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Small assay datasets can be amplified into design pressure through an oracle, lowering the wet-lab data volume needed to start a campaign.
insights.locator: Fig. 3: ProteinGuide guides ESM3 with assay-informed predictive models

themes.theme: Guidance on abstract labels, not just fitness

insights.claim: ProteinGuide can steer ESM3 with an enzyme-class (EC) predictor to generate sequences that an independent oracle classifies into the target enzyme class, with generated sequences additionally filtered for predicted foldability at pLDDT >= 0.8.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Conditioning on functional annotation classes rather than measured fitness opens de novo enzyme discovery for classes with no assay data — relevant to industrial-enzyme and biomanufacturing plays.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1, Guiding ESM3 with enzyme annotations

insights.claim: The same machinery guides ESM3 to produce backbone structures belonging to specified CATH fold classes that are also designable at self-consistency RMSD <= 2 A, so a sequence model can be steered to a structural target without a structure-generation model.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Erodes the boundary between sequence and structure design stacks; teams need not license a separate structure-diffusion model for fold-targeted design.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2, Guiding ESM3 to generate backbone structures with CATH fold class annotations

insights.claim: Guidance performance was probed by masking increasing fractions of an existing enzyme sequence and measuring how often the redesign is reclassified into the target class, giving an explicit dial between conservative redesign and de novo generation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The mask-fraction dial is the practical knob for trading design risk against novelty in a real campaign; a useful spec question for any design vendor.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1d, Guidance performance when redesigning test set enzyme sequences

insights.claim: Beyond the paper code, the authors shipped a ProteinGen Python package and a periodically updated practical guide to library design with ProteinGuide, signaling an intent to make the method the default tooling layer rather than a one-off publication.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Free, maintained tooling commoditizes the guidance layer of protein design and pushes startup value toward proprietary assays and delivery.
insights.quote: We have also published a guide to using ProteinGuide (https://ishangaur.com/proteinguide/), which will be updated periodically with our latest practical tips for successful library design.

insights.claim: The author roster maps the commercial edge of this work: David Savage cofounded Scribe Therapeutics, Hunter Nisonoff is now an employee of Generate:Biomedicines, and Jennifer Listgarten was on the scientific advisory board of Fable Therapeutics.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Identifies the private companies with the earliest internal access to this guidance approach — Scribe on the editing side, Generate:Biomedicines on the generative-design side.
insights.quote: D.F.S. is a cofounder and scientific advisory board member of Scribe Therapeutics. H.N. is currently an employee of Generate:Biomedicines. J.L. was a scientific advisory board member of Fable Therapeutics.

insights.claim: Funding came substantially from national-security-adjacent sources — the Department of Energy's Lawrence Livermore BioSecure Science Focus Area under Secure Biosystems Design and the Office of Naval Research — alongside NIH, HHMI and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: US defense and energy agencies are directly funding controllable protein-generation methods, a signal that biosecurity policy and dual-use scrutiny will follow this capability.
